title: Common submodule comparison with smaller-support integral filtrations
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $i:W\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and put $\xi=i(\operatorname{genericPoint}W)$. Let $G$ be coherent [pqf-def-coherent], with support $i(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], with $\mathfrak m_\xi G_\xi=0$, and with a compatible one-dimensional $\kappa(\xi)$-module structure [def-weil-residue-field]. For any quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ specified by $W.\mathrm{IdealSheafData}$, either $i_*I$ is zero or there are $K,Q_1,Q_2$ and short exact sequences $0\to K\to G\to Q_1\to0$ and $0\to K\to i_*I\to Q_2\to0$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Each $Q_t$ admits a finite increasing chain of subobjects from zero to all of $Q_t$, with every successive cokernel isomorphic to $j_*J$ for some closed immersion $j:W'\to X$, integral $W'$, and quasi-coherent ideal $J$ on $W'$, where $j(W')\subsetneq i(W)$. No cohomology or properness hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Split on whether i_*I is zero. In the zero case take the first disjunct. Otherwise the common-submodule construction supplies monomorphisms a and d with coherent canonical cokernels whose supports are strict subsets of i(W).
Use the canonical cokernel projection for each monomorphism. Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_cokernel, together with the mono inclusion and epi cokernel projection, gives the two short exact sequences.

Apply exists_finitePresentation_integral_filtration to each finitely presented cokernel Q. Its ideal factors can be zero. Define P to mean being an integral closed pushforward of a nonzero ideal. This property is invariant under isomorphism. The module of the zero ideal is zero: each stalk germ restricts to an affine neighborhood, where the ideal inclusion has zero image and is injective, so that germ vanishes; stalks detect zero objects. Pushforward preserves zero objects. Replace every zero-ideal factor by its empty filtration; every other factor already has P. Apply finite_filtration_refinement to obtain a chain with only nonzero ideal factors. This proves the private nonzero-filtration helper without an additional hole.

Prove locally in Lean that an integral-ideal subquotient j_*J of Q has image j(Wprime) contained in Supp Q. Coherence gives a closed support by the coherent/finite-type equivalence and finite_type_module_support_closed. At the image of the generic point the ideal stalk is nontrivial, as is its pushforward stalk by closedImmersion_pushforward_stalks. The forgetful functor from module sheaves preserves finite limits and colimits, as does the abelian-group sheaf stalk functor of Mathlib.Topology.Sheaves.Abelian. If Q had zero stalk there, injectivity of the subobject stalk inclusion and surjectivity of the stalk cokernel projection would make the subquotient stalk zero, contradicting the factor isomorphism. The generic point therefore belongs to Supp Q. Continuity of j and genericPoint_specializes put every point of j(Wprime) in this closed support. Transitivity with Supp Q strictly contained in i(W) gives the required strict image containment.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01YH and 01YF; A2 makes the subquotient support argument explicit using the generic point and closedness
